html:
The Clackamas are a Chinookan people of northwestern Oregon, living along the Clackamas River and the lower Willamette River near Willamette Falls.

The falls were one of the great salmon fishing places of the region, shared with the Kalapuya and Molalla and close to the trade of the Columbia River. They spoke a dialect of Upper Chinook, like the Wasco and Wishram upriver. Disease brought by the fur trade killed most of them in the 1830s. Settlers on the Oregon Trail then took their land, and after the Willamette Valley Treaty of 1855 the survivors were moved to the Grand Ronde reservation.
sum: The Clackamas are a Chinookan people of northwestern Oregon, living along the Clackamas River and the lower Willamette River near Willamette Falls.
